title: Weekly trading desk huddle
transcript:
Daniel Reyes: Morning everyone, let's get started. Agenda today: one, the blotter P&L discrepancy from last week. Two, OMS routing changes and the algo parameter review. Three, month-end and quarter-end prep. Four, the sales coverage handoff. Then any other business. Travis, you want to start with the blotter?
Travis Mitchell: Sure. So last Wednesday and Thursday, TradeBlotter was showing intraday P&L that was off versus what we saw at end of day. Biggest gap was around $180K on the equity book on Thursday afternoon. It corrected itself overnight, but the desk was making sizing decisions off a wrong number for a few hours.
Daniel Reyes: Do we know the root cause yet?
Travis Mitchell: Partially. TradeBlotter pulls fills from OMS and marks from PricingSvc. The fills were correct. The marks were stale on a handful of small-cap names, so it looks like a pricing lag upstream and not a blotter calculation bug. I raised a ticket with Technology and Omar Brown is looking at the MarketDataFeed side.
Sean Spencer: That matches what I saw. I pulled the mark timestamps for those names and some were sitting 15 to 20 minutes old while large caps were updating fine. Looks like a vendor conflation setting on the less liquid symbols.
Daniel Reyes: Okay. Sean, can you write up the list of affected symbols and the timestamps and attach it to the ticket so Omar has it? Then I want a staleness flag on the blotter if a mark is older than five minutes.
Sean Spencer: Yes, I can have the symbol list on the ticket by end of day today. The staleness flag needs a change from Technology, but I can draft the spec this week.
Daniel Reyes: Good. Action item for Sean, list today, spec by Friday. Derek, Erik, until that lands, please sanity check the blotter against your own screens on anything illiquid.
Derek Owens: Will do. I've been doing that already, honestly. On Thursday I caught it because my number for one of the biotech names looked too good to be true.
Erik Mcmillan: Same here. I'd also say we should not rely on the blotter for the mid-day risk check until the flag is in. Use the OMS position view instead.
Daniel Reyes: Agreed. That's the interim rule: for any decision on names below the liquidity threshold, cross-check OMS positions, not just blotter P&L. Moving on to routing. Travis?
Travis Mitchell: Two items. First, we're moving the default VWAP slicing for orders over 5% of ADV to the new schedule, which front-loads a bit less. Second, I'd like to tighten the participation cap on the opening auction orders. We had two orders last week that took more of the open than I was comfortable with.
Derek Owens: I'm fine with the cap. My concern is that on a gap day we might under-execute. Can we keep a manual override?
Travis Mitchell: Yes, the override stays. Anything above the cap needs a trader to confirm in OMS, and it gets logged.
Daniel Reyes: Good. Decision: new participation cap goes live Thursday, override stays with logging. Travis owns the change and will post the final parameters in the desk channel by Wednesday evening.
Sean Spencer: I can run a backtest on the last three months of opening orders to see what the cap would have done to slippage. Should have it by Wednesday noon.
Travis Mitchell: That would help, thanks Sean.
Daniel Reyes: Great. Next, quarter-end. Mary, you've been tracking the calendar.
Mary Wilson: Yes. Quarter-end is two weeks from Wednesday. Operations wants all allocations and any pending corrections in by 3 PM on the last business day, earlier than normal because of the settlement cutoffs. I also need everyone to clear the break list in the blotter before then. There are currently 14 open items, mostly stale allocations and a couple of unmatched give-ups.
Daniel Reyes: Fourteen is too many. Mary, can you split that list by owner and send it out today?
Mary Wilson: Will do. I'll tag each one with the trader and post it in the desk channel this afternoon, and I'll set a reminder for next Tuesday to check progress.
Erik Mcmillan: A few of those are mine from the August rebalance. I'll clear them by Friday.
Derek Owens: Two of them are mine. I'll get to them tomorrow.
Daniel Reyes: Good. Target is the break list under five by next Tuesday's huddle. Jessica, the coverage handoff.
Jessica Chen: Right. I'm out next Monday through Wednesday for a client event, so I need coverage for my institutional accounts. Two of the clients are active in the program trade space and tend to call early. I'd like Derek to be primary and Erik backup.
Derek Owens: Happy to. Can you send me the notes on how each one likes to receive color? Some prefer a call, some prefer chat.
Jessica Chen: Yes, I'll send a short handoff doc tomorrow. I'll also include the standing instructions on the axes we're showing so you don't need to ask.
Erik Mcmillan: I'm good as backup. Just flag anything with a settlement quirk.
Jessica Chen: Will do. One more thing from the client side. A couple of them asked about the blotter issue last week because we gave an indication using a wrong mark. I told them it was a data lag on our side and corrected the same day. Nothing else needed, but if someone else gets the question, that's the line.
Daniel Reyes: Good, keep that consistent. Any other business?
Mary Wilson: Quick one. The OMS login prompts were slower than usual on Monday morning for a few people. It cleared after a retry. If it repeats I'll raise it, since OMS depends on single sign-on.
Daniel Reyes: Yes, log it if it happens again with the time and who was affected. Okay, recap of owners. Sean: symbol list today, staleness flag spec by Friday, opening auction backtest by Wednesday noon. Travis: post cap parameters Wednesday evening, go live Thursday. Mary: send the break list by owner today. Erik and Derek: clear breaks by Friday. Jessica: coverage doc tomorrow. Thanks everyone, have a good week.
